topics.title: Bristol pursues wetland-city status
topics.summary: Bristol has launched a five-year effort to create and restore wetlands, aiming to reduce flood risk, support wildlife and broaden access to green and blue spaces.
topics.discussionPrompt: Imagine your neighborhood had room for a tiny wetland. Would you pick a rain garden, a pond, floating plants, or a wilder riverbank?

topics.title: Windfarm plans meet an unexpected boulder barrier
topics.summary: Greenpeace placed boulders to deter bottom trawling off Norfolk, but some landed at a planned windfarm site. The group and developer are discussing their exact placement.
topics.discussionPrompt: Two good goals collided here: protecting the seabed and building clean power. How would you get the groups around a table and find a practical fix?

topics.title: Microsoft services return after global outage
topics.summary: Microsoft says services have been restored after a major outage disrupted email, collaboration tools and public services in many countries, renewing attention on digital resilience.
topics.discussionPrompt: When an everyday app goes down, what backup habit saves the day: phone numbers on paper, offline notes, a second service, or simply taking a break?

topics.title: Starship test flight advances reusable-rocket work
topics.summary: SpaceX launched Starship on its 15th flight, with a planned orbital mission and return attempt. The booster splashed down after its tower return was aborted.
topics.discussionPrompt: Reusable rockets sound wonderfully ambitious. If you could reuse one thing from a huge project instead of throwing it away, what would it be?

topics.title: AI helps researchers read Gödel's notebooks
topics.summary: Researchers used AI to help decipher Kurt Gödel's dense shorthand notebooks, accelerating work on unpublished mathematical ideas and opening fresh material for historians of science.
topics.discussionPrompt: If an old box of notebooks could be decoded instantly, whose notes would you want to explore: a scientist, artist, relative, inventor, or someone else?

topics.title: Ireland opens its once-banned books archive
topics.summary: Ireland is moving thousands of historically banned books and censorship records to the National Archives, making a new resource available for readers and researchers.
topics.discussionPrompt: A library of once-hidden books is finally opening up. What kind of forgotten archive would you spend an afternoon exploring?

topics.title: A Darth Vader lightsaber sets an auction record
topics.summary: A screen-used Darth Vader lightsaber from two Star Wars films sold for nearly $5 million, setting a reported auction record for a Star Wars prop.
topics.discussionPrompt: If you could own one movie prop, would you choose something iconic, something useful, or a tiny background object with a great story?

topics.title: Eco architecture gets a global showcase
topics.summary: Architects highlighted five environmentally minded buildings that use approaches such as local materials, natural cooling and adaptive reuse while emphasizing visual design.
topics.discussionPrompt: Would you rather live in a timber tower, a breezy brick courtyard, or a cleverly reused old building? What would make it feel like home?

topics.title: Ohio salt-mine closure prompts winter planning
topics.summary: An Ohio salt mine beneath Lake Erie closed after water intrusion, raising questions about worker safety and how the region will secure road salt for winter.
topics.discussionPrompt: Winter planning is rarely glamorous. What small preparation makes the biggest difference when snow or ice suddenly changes everybody's routine?

topics.title: UK-EU plant-trade deal aims to trim border costs
topics.summary: A planned UK-EU agreement could simplify the movement of food, plants and animals, with businesses expecting less paperwork and fewer border delays.
topics.discussionPrompt: Behind every plant shop is a maze of transport and paperwork. What everyday item would surprise you to learn has the most complicated journey?
